info.title: Pawabase integrations: OAuth and Management API
info.description: Everything an external product calls to connect to Pawabase Cloud on a person's behalf: the OAuth 2.0 authorization server (`/oauth/*`) and the Management API (`/v1/*`). New to it? Start with [Apps, clients and connections](/integrations/clients) and the [REST quickstart](/integrations/rest-quickstart). The [integration SDK](/integrations/sdk) wraps all of this.

cloud.description: Pawabase Cloud. A self-hosted Cloud uses its own address (its `APP_URL`).

tags.name: OAuth
tags.description: Authorize, trade codes and refresh tokens, revoke. Run the token calls on your server.

get.description: The RFC 8414 document: the endpoints, grants, scopes and PKCE methods of this Pawabase Cloud. OAuth libraries that support discovery can be pointed at the issuer.

Step 1. Send the person's **browser** here (a 302). Pawabase checks the request, signs the person in if needed, shows the consent screen with an organization picker, and redirects to your `redirect_uri` with `?code=…&state=…` (approved) or `?error=access_denied&state=…` (cancelled). If the `client_id` or `redirect_uri` can't be vouched for, Pawabase never redirects: it answers `400` directly.

302.description: To the consent screen, and then back to your `redirect_uri`. Approved: `?code=pbo_…&state=…`. Cancelled: `?error=access_denied&error_description=The+person+declined.&state=…`. A problem with the request after the client and callback were checked: `?error=invalid_scope` (or `unsupported_response_type`, `invalid_request`).

example.error_description: That redirect_uri is not registered for this app.

parameters.name: redirect_uri
parameters.description: One of the app's registered callback URLs, exactly (loopback URLs may use any port). Optional only if the app has exactly one.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Space-separated scopes. Left out: every scope the app may ask for.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Strongly recommended. At least 16 random bytes you keep in the person's session and compare on return. Returned unchanged.

parameters.name: code_challenge
parameters.description: Recommended (required for public clients): base64url SHA-256 of your verifier, 43 characters. The verifier is 43–128 characters of `A–Z a–z 0–9 - . _ ~`.

post.description:
Steps 2 and 3, and platform apps. Run it **on your server**: it carries your client secret.

- `authorization_code`: trade the code from the callback (with the PKCE verifier) for tokens. A code is valid for 10 minutes and works **once**: a second use fails and ends the whole connection.
- `refresh_token`: trade the latest refresh token for a new pair. The old refresh token stops working, so save the new one first. A refresh token used twice ends the whole connection.
- `client_credentials`: a platform app's own token (no person, no refresh token).

**Client authentication:** HTTP Basic (`Authorization: Basic base64(client_id:client_secret)`, preferred), or `client_id` and `client_secret` in the body. A public client sends only `client_id` and relies on PKCE.

Rate limit: 300 requests a minute per client id and address, 1,200 a minute per address (shared with `/oauth/revoke`).

400.description: `invalid_grant` (the code or refresh token is unknown, used, expired, revoked, for another app or `redirect_uri`, the verifier doesn't match, or the connection was removed) or `unsupported_grant_type`.

401.description: `invalid_client`: unknown client id, wrong secret, or no secret and the code had no PKCE challenge. Carries `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="pawabase"`.

post.description: Ends the connection so it disappears from the organization's **Connected apps** list. Send the **refresh token** to end the whole connection (every token under it stops working). Send an access token to end only that token and the refresh token issued with it. Always `200 {}` for a known client, even for an unknown token (RFC 7009).

get.description: What the token is: its organization, role, scopes, and who or what it acts for. Needs no scope. Call it right after the token exchange, and link the connection to your own account by `user.id` (the email can change).

A list with the token's one organization, so code written for several works unchanged.

**Scope:** `organizations:read`. **Least role:** viewer.

The organization with its plan and usage. `{slug}` must be the token's own organization; any other is `404`.

**Scope:** `organizations:read`. **Least role:** viewer.

The organization's projects, newest first. Projects being deleted are left out. There is no paging.

**Scope:** `projects:read`. **Least role:** viewer.

post.description:
Answers `201` at once with the project in state `creating`; setting it up takes a few seconds to a minute (poll `GET /v1/projects/{ref}` no faster than every 2 seconds). With `app` (a marketplace app's slug) the app is installed as soon as the project is running.

**Scope:** `projects:write`. **Least role:** member.

get.description:
One project, plus its environments as the project's server reports them. `environments` is `null` when the server didn't answer in time, and absent when the project isn't `running`.

**Scope:** `projects:read`. **Least role:** viewer.

patch.description:
Change the name or description. The address (`slug`) never changes. An empty description clears it.

**Scope:** `projects:write`. **Least role:** admin.

delete.description:
Deletes the project **and all its data**: every environment, database, file and key. Answers at once; the project leaves lists immediately and is taken down in the background. **It cannot be undone.** A project with deletion protection on is refused with `409 protected`; integrations can't switch protection off.

**Scope:** `projects:write`. **Least role:** admin.

post.description:
Its data and settings stay; its API and Studio close. Pausing a paused project changes nothing; pausing one that isn't running or paused is `409 not_ready`.

**Scope:** `projects:write`. **Least role:** admin.

Restores a paused project.

**Scope:** `projects:write`. **Least role:** admin.

**Only a platform app's own token** (from `client_credentials`) may call it; any other token is `403 forbidden`. The project must be in the app's organization. The link is valid 7 days and works once: the person who opens it, signed in to Pawabase, moves the project into an organization they administer.

**Scope:** `projects:write`. **Least role:** admin.

Installs a marketplace app into an **existing, empty** project. Answers `202`; poll `GET /v1/projects/{ref}` and read `app.state` until it is `installed` or `failed` (`app.error` says why). Pawabase rehearses the install in a scratch environment first, so a failed install leaves the project as it was.

Refused at once: `409 has_app` (the project already has an app), `409 not_running` (paused or failed), `422 missing_values` (variables without defaults).

**Scope:** `projects:write`. **Least role:** admin.

get.description:
Pawabase's ready-made apps. `requires` lists plan features an app needs (for example `["ai"]`).

**Scope:** `projects:read`. **Least role:** viewer.

One app in full: its tables, flows, routes, and the **variables** it asks for, each with a name, description and default. Pass values for them as `values` when deploying.

**Scope:** `projects:read`. **Least role:** viewer.

Every key of the project. Never their secret values.

**Scope:** `project:read`. **Least role:** member.

post.description:
Creates a key in the project's first environment (or the one named by `?environment=<full name>`). **The key is in the answer once**, as `key`. A key belongs to the **project**, not the connection: disconnecting your app does not revoke keys it made.

**Scope:** `project:write`. **Least role:** admin.

201.description: The key, with its secret value

parameters.name: environment
parameters.description: The full name of the environment to make it in. Left out: the project's first.

role.description: `publishable` is safe in browsers (access rules apply); `secret` is server-only and bypasses access rules.

environments.description: `"all"`, or a list of environment names. Left out: only the one in the path.

get.description:
Reaches the same API Pawabase Studio uses, inside **one project**, so anything a person does in Studio a connected product can do: tables, records, access rules, flows, users, mail templates, buckets, secrets, keys, blueprints. Cloud checks the token, the scope and the person's role, signs a short-lived request for that project, and forwards it. Calls wait for the project's server up to **120 seconds**. An error from inside the project keeps its status and is given the Management API's shape (`error: project_error`), with the project's own body in `details`.

**Scope:** `project:read`. **Least role:** member.

200.description: The project server's own answer, unchanged: same status, body and content type (JSON, or a file such as a zip).

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: `{target}/{path}`. The target is `platform`, `auth`, `realtime`, `telemetry`, `gateway`, `object`, `avatar` or `document`. Most paths then start with `envs/{env}/…` (`platform`, `auth`) or `{env}/…`, where `{env}` is the project's `default_environment`.

bearerAuth.description: An OAuth access token, a personal access token (`pbp_…`), or a platform app's `client_credentials` token.

clientBasic.description: Your app's client id as the username and client secret as the password. A public client sends no secret and relies on PKCE.

scope.description: `client_credentials`: space-separated scopes. Left out: every scope the app may ask for.

client_id.description: In the body when not using HTTP Basic (and for public clients).

client_secret.description: In the body when not using HTTP Basic. A public client leaves it out.

refresh_token.description: Valid 30 days, used once. Absent for `client_credentials`.

organization.description: The slug of the organization the person picked.

details.description: What the API added: the scope that was needed, the plan limit, the fields that were wrong.

ref.description: How you name the project in `/v1/projects/{ref}`. The same as `slug`.

endpoints.description: Where the project's API answers, once running.

default_environment.description: The full name of the first environment; what Studio API paths use as `{env}`. `null` until running.

integration.description: Which app created the project through the API, if one did.

created_by_email.description: The person, or `app:<client id>` for a platform token.

region.description: A region code, where the Cloud offers a choice. Ignored where it doesn't.

app.description: A marketplace app's slug, installed as soon as the project is running.

values.description: With `app`: values for the app's variables.

Unauthorized.description: `unauthorized`: no token, an unknown or expired token, a revoked connection, a deleted app, or the person's account is gone.

Forbidden.description: `insufficient_scope` (`details.needed` names the scope) or `forbidden` (the person's role is too low, or they left the organization).

NotFound.description: `not_found`: the project, organization or marketplace app isn't in this organization.

example.message: That project in this organization was not found.

Invalid.description: `invalid` (`details` maps field names to problems) or `missing_values`.

PlanLimit.description: `plan_limit` (`details.limit`, `details.used`) or `plan_feature`: the organization's plan allows no more projects, or lacks a feature the app needs.

Unreachable.description: `unreachable`: the project's server could not be reached; try again in a minute.

example.message: The project's server did not answer.
